title: Sep-Latent: Separator Tokens as Natural Compression Anchors for Implicit Reasoning

paper.title: Sep-Latent: Separator Tokens as Natural Compression Anchors for Implicit Reasoning
paper.abstract: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable success in complex reasoning through explicit Chain-of-Thought (CoT), but the associated computational overhead and token verbosity remain significant barriers to efficiency. While implicit reasoning in continuous latent spaces offers a promising alternative, existing methods like Coconut and CODI often rely on fixed-length latent sequences and suffer from representational collapse. In this paper, we propose Sep-Latent , an adaptive implicit reasoning framework that utilizes separator tokens as structural semantic anchors. By introducing an Attention-Decay mechanism, we force the model to aggregate and compress reasoning logic into these anchors during training. We then align explicit and implicit pathways through multi-level distillation across all layers to ensure logical consistency. Crucially, Sep-Latent enables dynamic reasoning depth by adaptively terminating the latent thinking phase based on query complexity. Experimental results on the GSM8k-Aug benchmark show that Sep-Latent achieves an accuracy of 56.8% with an average of only 5.4 tokens, significantly outperforming prior fixed-length implicit models in efficiency while narrowing the performance gap with explicit CoT. Further analysis via PCA and symbolic variant testing confirms that our method ensures semantic grounding and exhibits superior robustness to perturbations.

sections.heading: 1 Introduction
sections.text: Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable success in complex reasoning tasks Touvron et al. (2023) ; Hurst et al. (2024) ; Shao et al. (2024) ; Yang et al. (2025) through explicit Chain-of-Thought (CoT) Wei et al. (2022) prompting. By generating intermediate textual steps, these models can decompose intricate problems into manageable logical sequences Sun et al. (2023) . However, explicit CoT is often bottlenecked by significant inference latency and computational overhead due to the generation of lengthy reasoning traces Yao et al. (2022) ; Xu et al. (2025c) . Furthermore, restricting reasoning to a discrete vocabulary space may lead to "over-thinking" and limits the model’s ability to utilize more flexible, continuous representations for internal computation Boix-Adsera et al. (2023) . To mitigate these issues, recent research has explored implicit reasoning Deng et al. (2024) ; Pfau et al. (2024) ; Goyal et al. (2023) , where the reasoning process is performed within the model’s continuous latent space. Pioneer works like Coconut Hao et al. (2022) and CODI Shen et al. (2025) demonstrate that CoT trajectories can be compressed into compact latent representations through distillation or curriculum learning. More recently, SIM-CoT Wei et al. (2025) introduced an extra supervised LLM to align implicit states with explicit reasoning steps to ensure logical consistency. Despite these advances, existing methods often utilize a fixed number of latent tokens, which lacks the flexibility to adapt to varying problem complexities and risks "semantic homogenization"—where latent states collapse into uninformative noise. Figure 1: Language models naturally allocate strong attention to separator tokens during reasoning. Increasing attention concentration on separator tokens preserves reasoning accuracy and perplexity with negligible performance variation Inspired by the observation that LLMs naturally prioritize separator tokens in 1 , we amplify attention concentration on these tokens through an attention-decay mechanism, enabling compact reasoning compression with negligible changes in perplexity and accuracy. We propose Sep-Latent , a framework utilizing Separator-guided semantic anchors and a progressive Attention-Decay mechanism. By selectively suppressing attention weights of non-separator tokens during training, we force the model to compress essential reasoning logic into structural tokens (e.g., ",","."). A dual-path distillation objective then aligns these compressed explicit representations with the implicit student path at both token and sequence levels.Our method introduces three significant improvements over existing frameworks: Attention-Decay Mechanism: We propose an attention-decay mechanism that progressively compresses intermediate reasoning information into separator tokens, enabling efficient latent reasoning while preserving long-range reasoning coherence. Online-Policy Distillation: We introduce an online-policy distillation strategy where the model continuously distills its own on-policy latent reasoning trajectories, improving reasoning stability while significantly reducing training memory overhead through self-distillation on compact latent states. Dynamic Implicit Exit: Sep-Latent enables adaptive termination. By applying an supervision on an exit token, the model dynamically adjusts reasoning depth based on query complexity and current reasoning states. Experimental results across multiple benchmarks, including math benchmark and commonsense benchmarks, demonstrate that Sep-Latent significantly outperforms previous implicit methods. On average, our method achieves a competitive accuracy of 56.8% on GSM8k Cobbe et al. (2021) using only 5.4 tokens, representing a more than two-fold increase in token efficiency compared to CODI and SIM-CODI. Furthermore, PCA visualizations confirm that our latent tokens are semantically diverse and well-grounded in the vocabulary space, effectively avoiding representational collapse. These findings establish Sep-Latent as a highly efficient and robust framework for internalized LLM reasoning.

sections.heading: 2.1 Implicit Reasoning
sections.text: In recent years, researchers have increasingly focused on implicit reasoning, motivated by the fact that explicit CoT can substantially increase inference cost in long-sequence settings and often produces redundant intermediate steps Zhang et al. (2025b) ; Li et al. (2025) . To address this, a growing body of work enables LLMs to perform reasoning in a continuous latent space, thereby avoiding the need to explicitly generate CoT text Strobl et al. (2024) ; Merrill and Sabharwal (2024) . To preserve reasoning capability without generating CoT, existing methods largely follow two directions: representation alignment and latent-trajectory learning. ICoT Deng et al. (2023) promotes the internalization of reasoning by aligning hidden states between a teacher model that generates CoT and a student model that outputs answers directly, using intermediate-representation supervision. Stepwise Internalization Deng et al. (2024) further proposes a staged fine-tuning procedure that gradually removes intermediate reasoning supervision, encouraging the model to internalize the reasoning process. In parallel, Coconut Hao et al. (2024) is among the first to distill explicit reasoning traces into a continuous latent space to learn latent reasoning; subsequent work Xu et al. (2025b) ; Su et al. (2025) continue to explore latent-space reasoning, yet still relies on explicit CoT generation during training or inference. SIM-COT Wei et al. (2025) additionally introduces supervised alignment between implicit reasoning and explicit thought steps to enhance reasoning consistency and accuracy. In contrast to prior methods, we introduce an attention-decay mechanism that organizes reasoning information in latent space through hierarchical structural guidance and semantic compression constraints, thereby enabling structured, controllable, and efficient implicit reasoning.

sections.heading: 2.2 Online-Policy Knowledge Distillation
sections.text: Knowledge distillation (KD) Gou et al. (2021) ; Xu et al. (2024) compresses models by transferring behavioral or representational knowledge from a teacher to a student, and has recently expanded from output-level distillation to distilling the reasoning process itself Hsieh et al. (2023) ; Ho et al. (2023) . System 2 Distillation Yu et al. (2024) proposes a self-distillation framework in which the same model alternates between teacher and student roles across stages and converts deep, explicit System-2 reasoning such as Tree-of-Thought or CoT into fast, heuristic System-1 reasoning. CODI Shen et al. (2025) compresses complex CoT trajectories into compact latent representations via iterative self-distillation, thereby enabling implicit reasoning. UnDIAL Dong et al. (2025) further employs self-distillation to preserve the model’s original behavioral characteristics. TwT Xu et al. (2025a) introduces a three-stage habitual-reasoning distillation framework that uses multi-teacher guidance and dual-criterion sampling and compresses explicit reasoning into latent capabilities. Building on these advances, we propose a joint reasoning optimization framework that jointly trains the model in explicit and implicit reasoning modes and enforces semantic consistency between them under structured supervision, which enables smooth knowledge transfer across the two reasoning pathways.

sections.heading: 3 Method
sections.text: Figure 2: Algorithm of Sep-Latent: As the training epochs proceed, LLM pays less and less attention to the reasoning step, and the information is gradually compressed into <sep>. It should be noted that although the figure uses two LLMS to illustrate the algorithm, there is actually one model during the actual training process. As shown in Fig. 2 , we propose a multi-stage training curriculum that transitions from Explicit Chain-of-Thought (CoT) to Implicit Reasoning by utilizing Separator Tokens (e.g. "\n", ",", ".") as semantic anchors. The core of this method involves a progressive Attention-Decay mechanism that encourages the model to compress semantic information from reasoning steps into these anchor tokens.

sections.heading: 4.1 Training Datasets
sections.text: Recent studies indicate that fine-tuning models with the GSM8k-Aug Deng et al. (2023) dataset can significantly enhance the model’s reasoning capabilities in mathematical tasks. GSM8k-Aug is an augmented dataset derived from the original GSM8k Cobbe et al. (2021) , expanded to approximately 385k examples with GPT-4. The dataset is processed to remove natural language reasoning chains, intending to force the model to internalize the intermediate reasoning process into specific mathematical calculations rather than discrete textual tokens. We present examples of the data used for explicit and implicit reasoning training in the appendix B.1 .

sections.heading: 4.2 Evaluation Benchmarks
sections.text: To evaluate the robustness and generalization of Sep-Latent, we conduct comprehensive evaluations across multiple benchmark categories: GSM8k Cobbe et al. (2021) serves as the in-domain test set, while MultiArith, SVAMP Patel et al. (2021) , and GSM-Hard Gao et al. (2023) are used to assess out-of-domain mathematical reasoning under structural and numerical distribution shifts. We further evaluate logical and commonsense reasoning capabilities using LogiQA Liu et al. (2020) , CSQA Talmor et al. (2018) , and StrategyQA Geva et al. (2021) . Finally, we include GSM-SYM Mirzadeh et al. (2024) to test the stability of our framework against symbolic perturbations. Detailed dataset distributions are provided in Appendix B.2 .

sections.heading: 4.3 Baselines
sections.text: To provide a comprehensive comparison, we evaluate our method against the following representative baselines:(1) SFT-COT: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on CoT-annotated data, LLMs will output an explicit reasoning chain before outputing the answer.(2) SFT-Direct: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) only on the answer, LLMs will direct output the answer without any thinking. (3) Coconut Hao et al. (2022) : By curriculum learning, LLMs gradually replace textual steps by latent expression. (4) CODI Shen et al. (2025) : By using knowledge distillation to align the hidden states of the answer of implict LLMs to explicit LLMs. (5) SIM-COT Wei et al. (2025) : An auxiliary model is introduced to decode the latent space reasoning of the original method so as to supervise the intermediate process. We follow the training setup of the previous and employ our experiments on Llama3-1B/3B/8B Dubey et al. (2024) , the detailed baselines setting are provided in Appendix C .

sections.text: We report the result of Llama3.2-1B and Qwen3-0.6B in Table 1 , in terms of in-domain performance on the GSM8k-Aug test set, Sep-Latent demonstrates a significant competitive advantage over existing implicit reasoning frameworks. Our method achieves an accuracy of 56.8%, marking a substantial improvement of +4.5% over the current state-of-the-art distillation method, SIM-CODI (52.3%). When compared against SIM-CODI (52.3%), which incorporates advanced step-level supervision, Sep-Latent maintains a performance edge. Most importantly, our approach effectively bridges the performance gap between implicit and explicit reasoning, nearing the accuracy of the SFT-CoT baseline (56.2%). These results demonstrate that Sep-Latent outperforms SIM-based frameworks while eliminating the need for auxiliary decoding models, thereby significantly reducing memory overhead. sections.heading: 5.2 Out-of-Domain Reasoning
sections.text: Math problems of different difficulties. Results in Table 1 underscore the superior generalization of Sep-Latent. This advantage is particularly evident in challenging scenarios like GSM-Hard, where Sep-Latent reaches 13.1% accuracy. On SVAMP, our model shows heightened resilience to structural perturbations with 62.0% accuracy, surpassing both baselines. Furthermore, on MultiArith, Sep-Latent maintains a high performance of 95.7%, nearly matching the explicit SFT-CoT teacher (96.7%) while remaining significantly more efficient. Variant Mathematical Reasoning. Traditional explicit reasoning are proved to be fragile when facing variant mathematical, this could be due to data leakage during the pre-training phase or a misplaced focus on irrelevant conditions. As illustrated in Figure 3 , Sep-Latent consistently demonstrates superior robustness compared to the explicit SFT-CoT baseline across all symbolic variant benchmarks. By shifting computation into the continuous latent space and bypassing the need for deterministic textual traces, Sep-Latent effectively mitigates the performance degradation typically caused by superficial perturbations in problem statements. These results suggest that implicit reasoning fosters a more generalized understanding of mathematical logic, making the model less susceptible to the linguistic biases or irrelevant textual cues that often plague explicit chain-of-thought methods. sections.heading: 5.3 Efficiency
sections.text: Figure 5: Comparative Analysis of Training Overhead: GPU Memory vs. Training Time Marker size is proportional to model accuracy (ACC), with larger bubbles representing better performance As shown in Figure 5 , we compare methods in training time, GPU memory usage, and accuracy (bubble size). Sep-Latent consistently lies in the best efficiency region, achieving competitive accuracy (56.8%) with substantially lower training cost than implicit reasoning methods such as Coconut and CODI. Sep-Latent is also highly token-efficient at inference, requiring only 5.4–5.7 tokens on average, compared with 11.9–13.4 for existing implicit methods and over 23 for SFT-CoT. This efficiency comes from our adaptive reasoning mechanism, where the model learns to emit a termination marker through ℒ i ​ m ​ p ​ _ ​ c ​ e \mathcal{L}_{imp\_ce} and ℒ d ​ i ​ s ​ t ​ _ ​ s ​ e ​ p \mathcal{L}_{dist\_sep} , reducing redundant computation while maintaining strong accuracy.

sections.heading: 6.1 Scaling to Larger Backbone
sections.text: To evaluate the scalability of our framework, we extend the evaluation to larger models within the Llama3 family: Llama3.2-3B-Instruct and Llama3.1-8B-Instruct. The results shown in Table 2 indicate Sep-Latent achieves an in-domain accuracy of 64.7% on the Llama3-3B, significantly outperforming CODI (60.8%) and SIM-CODI (62.3%) while maintaining superior token efficiency with only 5.5 tokens. This trend continues with the Llama3-8B, where our method reaches 68.8% in-domain accuracy. Notably, across all model scales, Sep-Latent maintains a nearly constant and remarkably low token consumption (5.5–5.7 tokens), whereas other implicit methods require significantly more overhead. These findings demonstrate that our adaptive latent reasoning mechanism retains its efficiency advantages even as the underlying backbone capacity scales.

sections.heading: 6.2 Necessity of Attention-Decay
sections.text: Figure 6: The ablation studies about Attention-Decay Mechanism We evaluated the Attention-Decay mechanism and separator token distillation by repeating each experiment 10 times using top-5 sampling (Figure 6 ). These quantitative results are also summarized in Table 1 . The significant performance drop when applying distillation without decay (green line) suggests that, lacking an explicit attention constraint, separator representations fail to capture the underlying reasoning process, introducing noise rather than guidance. Conversely, implementing decay without distillation (red line) reconfigures attention flow but lacks explicit process-based supervision, which limits its impact on accuracy. The synergy in our full method confirms that Attention-Decay provides the essential structural foundation for separator distillation to meaningfully represent and transfer reasoning logic.

sections.heading: 6.3 Distributions of Latent Tokens
sections.text: Recent Studies point out the implicit reasoning (Coconut) is not really thinking Zhang et al. (2025a) , it just generates isolated "pause" tokens. We therefore conducted a similar experiment. The PCA visualization in Figure 4 shows that Sep-Latent tokens maintain high-quality representations rather than collapsing into uninformative latent states. Unlike drifting implicit representations, our latent tokens remain close to the vocabulary manifold, indicating strong semantic grounding. Moreover, the clearly separated token distributions suggest that different latent tokens encode distinct reasoning computations, forming a semantically structured reasoning space.

sections.heading: 7 Conclusions
sections.text: In this paper, we introduced Sep-Latent, a framework for adaptive internalized reasoning that achieves high logical rigor with extreme token efficiency. By utilizing Attention-Decay and separator tokens as semantic anchors, we successfully compress explicit reasoning chains into a structured latent space. Our dual-path distillation ensures that this implicit pathway maintains accuracy without the overhead of textual generation. Crucially, Sep-Latent enables dynamic reasoning depth, allowing the model to autonomously adjust its latent tokens. This reduces consumption to an average of 5.4 tokens on GSM8k while remaining robust against representational collapse. Our approach represents a significant step toward developing efficient, autonomous reasoning agents that scale effectively across architectures.

sections.heading: Limitations
sections.text: Despite its efficiency and robustness, Sep-Latent has several limitations. First, while our method narrows the performance gap, it does not yet fully surpass the explicit SFT-CoT baseline in accuracy. This suggests that textual chains still provide a more stable supervision signal for certain complex logical tasks that are difficult to capture entirely in the latent space. Second, our sampling analysis reveals that the model often contains the correct answer within its output distribution even when greedy decoding fails. This indicates that the reasoning logic is present, but the model could benefit from Reinforcement Learning (RL) to better align the latent path with the correct solution.

sections.heading: B.2 Benchmark Distribution
sections.text: GSM-Aug is the training dataset we use, which is an augmented variant of GSM8K. It expands the original 8.5k training problems to approximately 385k examples through techniques such as paraphrasing, numerical resampling, and synthetic generation using GPT-4. The reasoning steps distribution of it are shown in Figure 7 . Figure 7: The reasoning steps distribution of training data. Most problems involve 1-4 steps and all the data are used for our training. SVAMP is an out-of-domain benchmark designed to test the model’s structural robustness. It consists of elementary-level math word problems that introduce variations in question phrasing and problem structure to challenge the model’s reliance on superficial patterns. GSM-Hard serves as a challenging out-of-domain evaluation set where numerical values in GSM8k problems are replaced with significantly larger magnitudes. This dataset specifically assesses the model’s ability to generalize its mathematical reasoning capabilities to more complex arithmetic scenarios. GSM-SYM is a specialized out-of-domain benchmark that introduces symbolic perturbations and variants to the original problems. It is employed to test the stability of reasoning models against subtle linguistic or symbolic changes that do not alter the underlying logic. LogiQA is a dataset for complex logical reasoning, derived from multiple-choice questions in the National Civil Service Examination. It evaluates the model’s capacity for high-level deductive and inductive reasoning. CommonsenseQA (CSQA) is a large-scale dataset used to assess general world knowledge and commonsense reasoning. It requires models to choose the correct answer by leveraging latent common sense information beyond the provided text. StrategyQA focuses on implicit reasoning tasks where the required reasoning path is not explicitly stated. Models must infer the correct multi-step strategy and execute the corresponding logical jumps to answer the questions accurately. Figure 8: The baselines used in our paper.

sections.heading: Appendix C implementation Details
sections.text: We implement Sep-Latent using the Hugging Face transformers library and accelerate training via DeepSpeed ZeRO-3. All experiments are conducted on a cluster of H20 GPUs. We fine-tune the model for 3 epochs with a total batch size of 128 and an initial learning rate of 1e-4. The learning rate is governed by a linear warmup followed by a cosine annealing scheduler to ensure stable convergence. We choose "\n" as our <sep> token. A key component of our training is the curriculum scheduling of the Attention-Decay factor ( γ \gamma ). To facilitate a smooth transition from standard explicit reasoning to the compressed semantic anchor phase, we employ a dynamic decay strategy during the first epoch. Specifically, γ \gamma starts at 1.0 (standard attention) and follows a cosine decay schedule until it reaches a predefined target value (e.g., 0.1) by the end of the first epoch. For the remaining two epochs, γ \gamma is maintained at this constant target value. This curriculum ensures that the model first learns the fundamental logical mappings before being forced to aggregate information into the separator tokens, thereby stabilizing the multi-level distillation process ( ℒ d ​ i ​ s ​ t ​ _ ​ s ​ e ​ p \mathcal{L}_{dist\_sep} ).

Affiliation: College of Computer Science and Technology, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, China Jian Wu 1 1 footnotemark: 1 Affiliation: College of Computer Science and Technology, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, China Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable success in complex reasoning through explicit Chain-of-Thought (CoT), but the associated computational overhead and token verbosity remain significant barriers to efficiency. While implicit reasoning in continuous latent spaces offers a promising alternative, existing methods like Coconut and CODI often rely on fixed-length latent sequences and suffer from representational collapse. In this paper, we propose Sep-Latent , an adaptive implicit reasoning framework that utilizes separator tokens as structural semantic anchors. By introducing an Attention-Decay mechanism, we force the model to aggregate and compress reasoning logic into these anchors during training. We then align explicit and implicit pathways through multi-level distillation across all layers to ensure logical consistency. Crucially, Sep-Latent enables dynamic reasoning depth by adaptively terminating the latent thinking phase based on query complexity. Experimental results on the GSM8k-Aug benchmark show that Sep-Latent achieves an accuracy of 56.8% with an average of only 5.4 tokens, significantly outperforming prior fixed-length implicit models in efficiency while narrowing the performance gap with explicit CoT. Further analysis via PCA and symbolic variant testing confirms that our method ensures semantic grounding and exhibits superior robustness to perturbations. 1 Introduction Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable success in complex reasoning tasks Touvron et al. (2023) ; Hurst et al. (2024) ; Shao et al. (2024) ; Yang et al. (2025) through explicit Chain-of-Thought (CoT) Wei et al. (2022) prompting. By generating intermediate textual steps, these models can decompose intricate problems into manageable logical sequences Sun et al. (2023) . However, explicit CoT is often bottlenecked by significant inference latency and computational overhead due to the generation of lengthy reasoning traces Yao et al. (2022) ; Xu et al. (2025c) . Furthermore, restricting reasoning to a discrete vocabulary space may lead to "over-thinking" and limits the model’s ability to utilize more flexible, continuous representations for internal computation Boix-Adsera et al. (2023) . To mitigate these issues, recent research has explored implicit reasoning Deng et al. (2024) ; Pfau et al. (2024) ; Goyal et al. (2023) , where the reasoning process is performed within the model’s continuous latent space. Pioneer works like Coconut Hao et al. (2022) and CODI Shen et al. (2025) demonstrate that CoT trajectories can be compressed into compact latent representations through distillation or curriculum learning. More recently, SIM-CoT Wei et al. (2025) introduced an extra supervised LLM to align implicit states with explicit reasoning steps to ensure logical consistency. Despite these advances, existing methods often utilize a fixed number of latent tokens, which lacks the flexibility to adapt to varying problem complexities and risks "semantic homogenization"—where latent states collapse into uninformative noise. Figure 1: Language models naturally allocate strong attention to separator tokens during reasoning. Increasing attention concentration on separator tokens preserves reasoning accuracy and perplexity with negligible performance variation Inspired by the observation that LLMs naturally prioritize separator tokens in 1 , we amplify attention concentration on these tokens through an attention-decay mechanism, enabling compact reasoning compression with negligible changes in perplexity and accuracy. We propose Sep-Latent , a framework utilizing Separator-guided semantic anchors and a progressive Attention-Decay mechanism. By selectively suppressing attention weights of non-separator tokens during training, we force the model to compress essential reasoning logic into structural tokens (e.g., ",","."). A dual-path distillation objective then aligns these compressed explicit representations with the implicit student path at both token and sequence levels.Our method introduces three significant improvements over existing frameworks: Attention-Decay Mechanism: We propose an attention-decay mechanism that progressively compresses intermediate reasoning information into separator tokens, enabling efficient latent reasoning while preserving long-range reasoning coherence. Online-Policy Distillation: We introduce an online-policy distillation strategy where the model continuously distills its own on-policy latent reasoning trajectories, improving reasoning stability while significantly reducing training memory overhead through self-distillation on compact latent states. Dynamic Implicit Exit: Sep-Latent enables adaptive termination. By applying an supervision on an exit token, the model dynamically adjusts reasoning depth based on query complexity and current reasoning states. Experimental results across multiple benchmarks, including math benchmark and commonsense benchmarks, demonstrate that Sep-Latent significantly outperforms previous implicit methods. On average, our method achieves a competitive accuracy of 56.8% on GSM8k Cobbe et al. (2021) using only 5.4 tokens, representing a more than two-fold increase in token efficiency compared to CODI and SIM-CODI. Furthermore, PCA visualizations confirm that our latent tokens are semantically diverse and well-grounded in the vocabulary space, effectively avoiding representational collapse. These findings establish Sep-Latent as a highly efficient and robust framework for internalized LLM reasoning. 2 Related Work 2.1 Implicit Reasoning In recent years, researchers have increasingly focused on implicit reasoning, motivated by the fact that explicit CoT can substantially increase inference cost in long-sequence settings and often produces redundant intermediate steps Zhang et al. (2025b) ; Li et al. (2025) . To address this, a growing body of work enables LLMs to perform reasoning in a continuous latent space, thereby avoiding the need to explicitly generate CoT text Strobl et al. (2024) ; Merrill and Sabharwal (2024) . To preserve reasoning capability without generating CoT, existing methods largely follow two directions: representation alignment and latent-trajectory learning. ICoT Deng et al. (2023) promotes the internalization of reasoning by aligning hidden states between a teacher model that generates CoT and a student model that outputs answers directly, using intermediate-representation supervision. Stepwise Internalization Deng et al. (2024) further proposes a staged fine-tuning procedure that gradually removes intermediate reasoning supervision, encouraging the model to internalize the reasoning process. In parallel, Coconut Hao et al. (2024) is among the first to distill explicit reasoning traces into a continuous latent space to learn latent reasoning; subsequent work Xu et al. (2025b) ; Su et al. (2025) continue to explore latent-space reasoning, yet still relies on explicit CoT generation during training or inference. SIM-COT Wei et al. (2025) additionally introduces supervised alignment between implicit reasoning and explicit thought steps to enhance reasoning consistency and accuracy. In contrast to prior methods, we introduce an attention-decay mechanism that organizes reasoning information in latent space through hierarchical structural guidance and semantic compression constraints, thereby enabling structured, controllable, and efficient implicit reasoning. 2.2 Online-Policy Knowledge Distillation Knowledge distillation (KD) Gou et al. (2021) ; Xu et al. (2024) compresses models by transferring behavioral or representational knowledge from a teacher to a student, and has recently expanded from output-level distillation to distilling the reasoning process itself Hsieh et al. (2023) ; Ho et al. (2023) . System 2 Distillation Yu et al. Moreover, the clearly separated token distributions suggest that different latent tokens encode distinct reasoning computations, forming a semantically structured reasoning space. 7 Conclusions In this paper, we introduced Sep-Latent, a framework for adaptive internalized reasoning that achieves high logical rigor with extreme token efficiency. By utilizing Attention-Decay and separator tokens as semantic anchors, we successfully compress explicit reasoning chains into a structured latent space. Our dual-path distillation ensures that this implicit pathway maintains accuracy without the overhead of textual generation. Crucially, Sep-Latent enables dynamic reasoning depth, allowing the model to autonomously adjust its latent tokens. This reduces consumption to an average of 5.4 tokens on GSM8k while remaining robust against representational collapse. Our approach represents a significant step toward developing efficient, autonomous reasoning agents that scale effectively across architectures. Limitations Despite its efficiency and robustness, Sep-Latent has several limitations. First, while our method narrows the performance gap, it does not yet fully surpass the explicit SFT-CoT baseline in accuracy. This suggests that textual chains still provide a more stable supervision signal for certain complex logical tasks that are difficult to capture entirely in the latent space. Second, our sampling analysis reveals that the model often contains the correct answer within its output distribution even when greedy decoding fails. This indicates that the reasoning logic is present, but the model could benefit from Reinforcement Learning (RL) to better align the latent path with the correct solution. SVAMP is an out-of-domain benchmark designed to test the model’s structural robustness. It consists of elementary-level math word problems that introduce variations in question phrasing and problem structure to challenge the model’s reliance on superficial patterns. GSM-SYM is a specialized out-of-domain benchmark that introduces symbolic perturbations and variants to the original problems. It is employed to test the stability of reasoning models against subtle linguistic or symbolic changes that do not alter the underlying logic. LogiQA is a dataset for complex logical reasoning, derived from multiple-choice questions in the National Civil Service Examination. It evaluates the model’s capacity for high-level deductive and inductive reasoning. CommonsenseQA (CSQA) is a large-scale dataset used to assess general world knowledge and commonsense reasoning. It requires models to choose the correct answer by leveraging latent common sense information beyond the provided text. Appendix C implementation Details We implement Sep-Latent using the Hugging Face transformers library and accelerate training via DeepSpeed ZeRO-3. All experiments are conducted on a cluster of H20 GPUs. We fine-tune the model for 3 epochs with a total batch size of 128 and an initial learning rate of 1e-4. The learning rate is governed by a linear warmup followed by a cosine annealing scheduler to ensure stable convergence. We choose "\n" as our <sep> token. A key component of our training is the curriculum scheduling of the Attention-Decay factor ( γ \gamma ). To facilitate a smooth transition from standard explicit reasoning to the compressed semantic anchor phase, we employ a dynamic decay strategy during the first epoch. Specifically, γ \gamma starts at 1.0 (standard attention) and follows a cosine decay schedule until it reaches a predefined target value (e.g., 0.1) by the end of the first epoch. For the remaining two epochs, γ \gamma is maintained at this constant target value. This curriculum ensures that the model first learns the fundamental logical mappings before being forced to aggregate information into the separator tokens, thereby stabilizing the multi-level distillation process ( ℒ d ​ i ​ s ​ t ​ _ ​ s ​ e ​ p \mathcal{L}_{dist\_sep} ).
